findings.area: scope / ADR-026 clause 1 (work worker subject substitution)
findings.summary: The LibraryWorkWorker logs now replace the entire WorkItemKey text, dropping the bounded connection identity and image surface from both Debug records; ADR-026 clause 1 authorizes replacing only the Jellyfin item identifier, and the task is scoped to threading the subject only.
findings.detail: Before the change the worker emitted `Work item {item.Key}` where `WorkItemKey.ToString()` is `WorkItemKey(<ItemId:N>, <ConnectionId ?? "*">, <Surface.Key>)` (src/ArrTags/Updates/WorkItemKey.cs:108-113). The change emits `Work item {LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId)}` (src/ArrTags/Updates/LibraryWorkWorker.cs:240,262), i.e. only the D-format item id. ADR-026 clause 1 says 'Log call sites that currently emit the Jellyfin item identifier emit a bounded log subject instead' and clause 3 labels the worker fallback '(item id only)'. '(item id only)' describes the subject value, not the whole record: every other site keeps its non-subject bounded context (provider kind, match status/method, error code) while replacing only the identifier, and the lifecycle site keeps its surrounding sentence while swapping only the identifier. The dropped values are explicitly allowed and non-secret bounded diagnostics (WorkItemKey doc: 'safe to retain as a queue key and diagnostic'; ADR-020 clause 4 permits connection identity), so this is diagnostic loss, not a redaction gain. It is also more than the subject-only scope: the worker line now carries less diagnostic information than before and no path is available to compensate. The worker disclosed the whole-key replacement in interpretations[2], but the stated basis does not show the ADR authorizes dropping the connection/surface components. Emitting the item-id subject while retaining the bounded connection/surface context would still satisfy the acceptance criterion and preserve the connection/surface diagnostics.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-026.md:43-47 (clause 1: replace the item identifier), :59-67 (clause 3: '(item id only)' subject; 'via WorkItemKey')
docs/decisions/ADR-020.md:48-54 (connection identity is an allowed, non-secret bounded value)
docs/implementation/15.2/worker-report.json interpretations[2] and known_limitations[0] (worker discloses dropping the WorkItemKey text)
src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsLifecycleService.cs:155-159 (contrast: the fallback site preserves its surrounding bounded context)
findings.recommended_action: Keep the item-id fallback as the subject but retain the bounded connection-scope and surface components in the processed/retry records (for example `Work item {subject} ({item.Key.ConnectionId ?? "*"}, {item.Key.Surface.Key}) ...`), and add an assertion pinning those components so the reduction cannot recur; alternatively record an explicit, cited decision that the worker record is intentionally item-id-only. Do not change the WorkItemKey type itself (coalescing identity must not change).

findings.area: acceptance criteria / worker evidence (metadata-read-failure catch path)
findings.summary: The reader-threw metadata-read-failure path is a distinct subject call site that no test exercises, yet the worker report and changelog claim both provider-error paths are verified.
findings.detail: MetadataReconciliationProcessor has two MetadataReadFailed emissions: the reader-threw catch (subject built at src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:159, written at :162) and the failed-read result (:181/:184). The worker report acceptance_criteria[1] states 'Both MetadataReadFailed paths ... build the subject' and cites LogRedactionTests as the evidence. DriveMetadataReadFailureAsync (tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogRedactionTests.cs, pathAvailable overload) sets `FakeMetadataReader.Result` to a failure result and never a throwing Handler; FakeMetadataReader.ReadAsync returns `Result ?? Handler(...)` (tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationFixtures.cs:93), so the catch block is never entered. I independently confirmed the mechanism by inspection; the separate test-quality review (docs/implementation/15.2/test-quality-review.json TQ-15.2-01) reached the same conclusion with a probe that reverted only the catch-path subject and still passed 125/125. The implementation of both paths is correct in the diff; the defect is the overstated verification claim plus the missing per-site proof for that emission path.
findings.recommended_action: Add one case (or theory) that drives the reader-threw catch with a FakeMetadataReader.Handler that throws, with a path-bearing and a pathless identity, asserting the file-name-only / item-id-fallback subjects; or narrow the worker report and changelog claims to the failed-read path actually covered.

findings.area: acceptance criteria / worker evidence (worker retry-scheduled path)
findings.summary: LibraryWorkWorker.LogRetryScheduled is a separate subject call site that no test drives, yet the worker report and changelog name it as covered.
findings.detail: The worker changed two sites, LogProcessed (src/ArrTags/Updates/LibraryWorkWorker.cs:240) and LogRetryScheduled (:262). WorkWorkerSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity drives DriveQueueAsync, which uses RecordingWorkItemProcessor (a double that always returns a non-retryable Completed result), so LogRetryScheduled is never reached; only LogProcessed is asserted. The worker report acceptance_criteria[4] and the changelog name 'processed and retry-scheduled' together. The implementation of both is correct in the diff; the gap is coverage of the retry site. The test-quality review independently recorded the same gap (TQ-15.2-02).
findings.recommended_action: Add a queue case whose processor returns a retryable result for one attempt so the WorkItemRetryScheduled record is emitted, and assert the item-id subject on it; or drop LogRetryScheduled from the coverage claim.

findings.area: architecture / ADR-026 clause 3 enumeration versus code
findings.summary: ADR-026 clause 3 lists 'ineligible' and 'connection unavailable' as discard sites where no identity exists, but in code those pre-publish discards run after identity creation and do have a path available; the implementation follows the enumeration.
findings.detail: In MetadataReconciliationProcessor, identity is created at src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:124, before the pre-publish eligibility (discard at :130) and connection-unavailable (discard at :142) checks, so a MediaLocation with a primary path can be available at those 2-arg Discard calls. ADR-026 clause 3 (docs/decisions/ADR-026.md:59-65) nonetheless names 'ineligible' and 'connection unavailable' in the group 'where it does not [have an identity]', and the implementation matches that enumeration: the two-argument Discard overload passes no path at those sites, and only the six publish-time changed-basis discards pass identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath. Because the task names the ADR-026 clause 3 enumeration as the governing decision, this is not a required change for 15.2; the ADR's characterization is simply inaccurate for those two (and the unlisted missing-provider-kind) pre-publish discards, and clause 1's general path-when-available rule would otherwise cover them.
findings.recommended_action: No change required for 15.2. Task 15.4's documentation reconciliation (or a follow-up ADR clarification) should reconcile clause 3's parenthetical with the actual call sites so clause 1 and clause 3 agree on whether those pre-publish discards should carry the path.

findings.summary: All six ADR-026 clause 3 site files are threaded with the correct subject forms, the four unchanged sites and LogSubject.cs are untouched, and logging changes are confined to the six sites.
findings.detail: git diff --name-only HEAD lists exactly the six production files (ArtworkGenerationCoordinator, ArrTagsLifecycleService, RadarrMetadataReader, SonarrMetadataReader, MetadataReconciliationProcessor, LibraryWorkWorker) plus LogRedactionTests and the three doc/state files. No change under ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader, WebhookIntakeService, WebhookAuthenticationFilter, or LibraryReconciliationService. src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs has no diff against HEAD (introduced at ba159c6). LogSubject.Create is invoked at exactly the nine production call sites ADR-026 clause 3 names (coordinator, two read-failure paths, Radarr/Sonarr LogMatch, the 3-arg Discard helper, and the two worker/lifecycle fallbacks). The coordinator reads request.MediaIdentity, which is non-nullable and guarded by ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull in the ArtworkGenerationRequest constructor, so no new NRE path is introduced; identity is non-null at the processor discard and reader sites.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs (no diff; only src usage of LogSubject.Create at the nine sites)
